title: Why Astro and Contentful make a fast, editable marketing site
description: How pre-rendering with Astro and a headless CMS gives you a site that is quick for visitors and easy for editors to change.
body:
Marketing sites have two jobs: load quickly and be easy to change. Astro and Contentful cover both.

## Pre-render everything

Astro renders pages to plain HTML at build time. Visitors get a document with no framework runtime, which keeps Core Web Vitals healthy.

## Let editors own the words

Contentful holds the copy. A publish triggers a rebuild, so the live site always reflects the content without a developer in the loop.

- Fast pages by default
- Structured, typed content
- A short path from edit to production

The trade-off is a build step between publishing and going live. For a marketing site, about a minute is a fair price.

title: Using AI agents in a real delivery workflow
description: What changes when an agent picks up well-scoped tickets, and the guardrails that keep humans in charge of what ships.
body:
Agents are most useful when the work is well scoped and the definition of done is written down.

## Guardrails first

A label gates what an agent may pick up, and a human reviews every deploy preview before merging.

## Write the issue for a reader with no context

State the outcome, link the content model and list what complete looks like. A good ticket helps people as much as it helps agents.

title: Typed content queries in TypeScript
description: A small pattern for fetching CMS content with typed queries, build-time caching and a safe local fallback.
body:
Keep each query in a module next to the type it returns.

```ts
const posts = await getBlogPosts();
```

Cache the promise once per build, fail loudly when credentials exist but the request fails, and fall back to local JSON only when they are missing.
